title: Long USO — WTI at $80 September Hike Trip Wire on Iran Blockade Resumption
entry: $115–122 (intraday $117.79). Enter at or below $119 to maintain full stop distance. WTI is at $79.56, within $0.44 of the $80 September hike trip wire. The 'Iran ceasefire over' declaration (Trump July 13) has materially changed the supply-risk calculus since the June 2026 ceasefire that depressed WTI to $68–70.
stop_loss: $106 daily close (~10% below $118 midpoint) — implies WTI has fallen back below $70 on one of: (1) a surprise Iran-US ceasefire announcement with Hormuz commercially re-opened above 70% of normal capacity, directly removing the supply-disruption premium; (2) OPEC+ emergency production increase above 1Mbpd offsetting Hormuz supply risk; or (3) US-Iran direct negotiations confirmed and Hormuz demilitarization commitment announced. Below $106, the structural oil thesis is invalidated.
targets: $127 — WTI breaks $83 and sustains for 3 sessions; Brent above $88 triggers shipping insurance exclusion-zone pricing for Gulf tanker routes; USO +7.8% from $118 entry; cover 40% of position in week 1–2

$137 — WTI pushes to $88–92 on Gulf state tanker incidents or IRGC naval interdiction; August CPI loading begins — oil at this level embeds 0.8–1.2 percentage points of upward pressure on August headline CPI (released August 12); USO +16.1% from entry; cover 40%

$149 — Full Hormuz-closure scenario: WTI above $95; Iranian naval action cuts 20–30% of global crude/LNG exports; US deploys additional carrier strike group to the Gulf; USO approaches 52-week high zone; +26.5%; hold final 20%
catalyst: Trump declared the Iran-US ceasefire 'over' on July 13, 2026, re-initiating Hormuz disruption risk. WTI has moved from ~$67 (post-ceasefire June levels) to $79.56 intraday on July 14 — within $0.44 of the $80 September hike trip wire. A sustained move above $80 before August 12 (the August CPI release date) would embed the oil price shock into August CPI, potentially converting the September FOMC from a 'data-dependent pause' to a near-certain rate hike.
thesis:
USO provides direct WTI crude oil exposure without the equity-specific risk that XLE and XOM carry. XLE is dominated by large-cap US producers whose stock performance also reflects Q3 earnings estimates, capex plans, and dividend coverage ratios; XOM carries Permian operating risk and LNG contract pricing risk. USO is pure commodity — it responds directly to WTI price movements, providing the cleanest expression of the Hormuz-disruption thesis.

WTI at $79.56 is the critical level. The $80 threshold has been flagged by the morning briefing routine as the 'September hike trip wire' because it embeds a structural oil supply shock into August CPI (released August 12). If WTI sustains above $80 for 5–10 trading days before the August BLS data collection cutoff, the headline August CPI will mechanically show 0.8–1.2 percentage points of energy contribution — turning what would be a 3.8% July CPI toward 4.6%+ in August. That trajectory removes any ambiguity about the September 2026 FOMC decision.

The June 2026 ceasefire-era WTI trough of $67–68 represented the market pricing Hormuz fully re-opened. That assumption is now invalidated by Trump's July 13 declaration. The re-pricing from $67 toward the pre-ceasefire Hormuz-disruption fair value of $85–88 is the base-case trade over 2–4 weeks. USO captures this directly without the earnings-calendar noise embedded in XLE and XOM.

The $80 level creates an accelerating positive feedback: above $80, September hike probability rises (from ~60% to 75%+), which is dollar-positive, which creates financial conditions tightening even before the FOMC acts. But the oil price itself continues to discount the Hormuz supply risk independently. The asymmetry is attractive: USO has $11 of downside to the stop ($106) and $31 of upside to Target3 ($149) — approximately 1:2.8 risk/reward across the full range.
bull_case: Hormuz partial closure confirmed (IRGC naval action against Gulf state tankers); WTI to $90+; USO to $149+ in 3–4 weeks. This is the asymmetric upside given the $12 stop distance vs the $31 blue-sky gain.
bear_case: Iran-US back-channel negotiations restart within 72 hours of today's 'ceasefire over' declaration; Hormuz threat is again defused by a Chinese- or Russian-mediated agreement; WTI reverses toward $72–74; stop triggered at $106 on USO. The prior ceasefire demonstrated how quickly oil can retrace when diplomatic resolution is announced.
invalidation: $106 USO daily close; OR Iran-US ceasefire announced with Hormuz commercially re-opened above 70% of normal capacity (WTI falls back below $70 immediately); OR OPEC+ emergency production increase of 1.5Mbpd+ that offsets Hormuz supply risk; OR WTI falls below $70 for two consecutive sessions on any reason (structural demand-destruction signal or supply-side reversal).
